title: Rozen Maiden
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: After cruelty from classmates, middle-schooler Jun Sakurada shuts himself in his room. A living doll, the imperious Shinku, arrives and makes him her servant, pulling him into the Alice Game, in which seven Rozen Maiden dolls fight to become the perfect doll. The dolls, his sister Nori and a class representative all push Jun to rejoin the world (Seven Seas blurb; ANN Spring 2025 Manga Guide).
life_message: Bonds with others, even demanding ones, can draw a hurt person out of isolation.

content.note: Dolls clash using human mediums (ANN); AniList Battle Royale; not a focus per reviewers.
ANN reviewer calls its moe indulgence 'unsavory' for its target audience; no sexual tags. Rated T.
Jun is a shut-in after classmates' cruelty (blurb; ANN; AniList Hikikomori, Rehabilitation).
Collector's edition; doll and Gothic Lolita aesthetic.

dominant: Recovery from isolation; rivalry among sister dolls; quest for perfection

frames.aligns: Community, sister and companions bring Jun back to life.

Ensouled dolls and contracts as spiritual imagery.

frames.aligns: Love that persists toward a withdrawn boy (Nori).
Restoration of a broken young man.
frames.concerns: Contracts binding a human to spirit-dolls.

frames.aligns: Vocation as Jun learns to serve others.

frames.concerns: Battles to the end between sisters.

frames.aligns: Family support and growth through trial.

Mental-health theme of withdrawal after bullying.
Duty, manners (Shinku's demands) and returning to school.

Objects with spirit, akin to tsukumogami.
Service (seva) pulls Jun out of ego.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Dolls fight for status in the Alice Game (blurb).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Shinku demands service and decorum (blurb, ANN 'imperious').

Civic vs kin.evidence: Sister Nori and the doll 'sisters' are the core bonds (ANN, MU Sibling Rivalry).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Jun made Shinku's servant; only one doll can become Alice (blurb).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Rococo, Gothic aesthetic and magic in modern Japan (ANN).

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Recovery and survival balance doll fashion and self-expression.

folkways.japan: Hikikomori withdrawal after school bullying is a recognized Japanese social issue, described as context.

delivery.evidence: ANN: dolls, class rep and Nori 'work hard to pull Jun out'; neither reviewer calls it preachy.
delivery.note: Recovery is carried by relationships and events rather than stated lessons.

winners_losers: Jun and the dolls who bond with him are sympathetic; isolation is the real opponent.
to_verify: This AniList entry is the original 2002-2007 run; Seven Seas is republishing it in collector's omnibuses, TokyoPop's edition is expired.
Later violence between dolls and Suigintou's role not confirmed from opened sources.
